subject: P95 spike in us-west — routing / fallback applied
messages:
From: Alyssa Barnes <alyssa.barnes@aurorabiotech.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:14:03 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 spike — us-west (started 08:50 PDT)

Hi Vivek / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sustained p95 generation time increase affecting about ~15% of our calls to hosted API in us-west starting ~08:50 PDT. Impact: conversational sessions with longer responses are timing out in our UI and some user flows are falling back to cached content. Sample request IDs: req_3b9f, req_3ba1, req_3bc4.

Traffic pattern looks normal (no obvious surge on our side). Can you confirm whether there are routing changes, queueing, or queued-back pressure on your end? This is affecting our clinical experiment UX.

Happy to jump on a quick bridge if helpful — we're on PST.

Thanks,
Alyssa Barnes
Head of Platform Ops
AuroraBio

[Attachment: aurorabiotech_sample_headers.txt (text/plain)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Barnes <alyssa.barnes@aurorabiotech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:28:10 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike — us-west (started 08:50 PDT)

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the quick report and example IDs. We see correlated p95 elevations in our telemetry for us-west starting 08:48 PDT. Our initial triage indicates an uneven routing shuffle between two edge pools that slightly increased queueing for generation-heavy requests (long-context chat).

Immediate actions we've taken:
- Enabled targeted fallback routing for AuroraBio to route new requests to the secondary capacity pool that has spare kernels (no model change)
- Temporarily increased per-customer concurrent slots for your account by 20% to reduce queuing
- Kicked off a live flush of prefix/KV cache for affected pools to eliminate hot-key stalls

Expected customer-visible change: p95 should start improving within ~5-7 minutes of reroute. We'll keep the fallback in place while we stabilize.

Can you confirm whether you still see UI timeouts after ~09:35 PDT? We'll keep you in the loop via this thread and the incident page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2028-0625-usw-p95

I'll also escalate to on-call to capture kernel/driver traces and follow up with a root-cause note.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: root_cause_snapshot.log (text/plain)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:45:22 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Sudden p95 spike — us-west (started 08:50 PDT)

Team — internal note and actions:
- Customer: AuroraBio (prod traffic).
- Symptom: p95 generation up ~2.5x for long-sequence chat calls.
- Immediate mitigation: routing fallback to secondary pool + +20% concurrency for this account (applied, customer notified).
- Next: capture kernel traces from pool-a, compare kernel selection logs vs pool-b (see attached diff).
- Ask: Ops, please snapshot the routing config at 08:40–09:10 and surface any autoscaler churn events. Also confirm whether we had any recent kernel/driver rollouts in us-west cluster in that window.

I'll draft a brief incident communication for the status page once we have probes and ETR. Please respond in-channel if you see a quick plan for permanent mitigation (route smoothing / hot-key prefetch).

— Vivek

Hi Vivek — thanks for the fast response and the mitigation. Our UX team reports p95 is back to expected levels as of 11:38 PDT and the timeouts cleared. We'll keep monitoring overnight and will report any anomalies.

Appreciate the clear comms and the temporary extra concurrency — it's helped our experiments continue running. Please send a short post-incident note with root cause and whether any customer-visible configuration will change (e.g., routing smoothing enabled by default).

Best,
Alyssa
